walkthroughs.body_html:
The UK was shaped by past ice sheets.

Glaciers carved U-shaped valleys, corries and aretes.

The Lake District is a classic example.

walkthroughs.h2: Rivers carry water from source to mouth in a
walkthroughs.body_html:
Rivers carry water from source to mouth in a drainage basin.

Energy and load change downstream, so does the channel.

Upstream: vertical erosion. Downstream: lateral erosion.

Across the lower course, meanders dominate.

Outer bends erode quickly, leaving a river cliff.

Inner bends slow down and drop sediment as a slip-off slope.

mcqs.q: Why do meanders migrate across a floodplain?
options: Meanders form because rivers flow around obstacles like rocks.
Hydraulic action is when the river dissolves rocks chemically.
Faster water on the outside of the bend causes erosion (river cliff); slower water on the inside causes deposition (slip-off slope) — over time the channel shifts laterally.
Meanders form because the river is going downhill very steeply.

mcqs.q: What is hydraulic action in a river?
options: Hydraulic action is when rocks in the river smash into each other.
The force of moving water itself compressing air into cracks in the river bank or bed, weakening rock until pieces break off — no sediment needed.
Abrasion is when wind erodes the glacier and plucking is when rain does.
Hydraulic action is when the river dissolves rocks chemically.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between glacial abrasion and plucking?
options: Abrasion and plucking are different words for the same process.
Abrasion: rock embedded in the glacier base scrapes the bedrock smooth, creating striations. Plucking: meltwater refreezes onto bedrock, then movement rips chunks of rock away.
Abrasion is when wind erodes the glacier and plucking is when rain does.
